.4. The claimants 7 and 8 have filed claim statement stating that the propositor late.
Venkataramanappa had four sons by name Sampanna, Veerachikkappa, Nagappa and Mudlappa died leaving behind the following legal heirs.
Sri. Sampanna died leaving behind Chikkahanumaiah and Nanjundappa.
Both Chikkahanumaiah and Nanjundappa died leaving behind Narasimhamurthy, Venkatarasappa, Doddagalappa, Chikkagalappa, Hanumaiah and Narasappa as legal heirs.
The second son L.A.C. No. 107/2014 C/w L.A.C. No. 108, 112 &113 of 2014 Veerachikkappa died leaving behind Arasappa, Chikkarasappa and Mudlappa.
Arasappa died leaving behind Venkatarasappa and Chikkarasappa.
The other sons Mudlappa and issue less.
The third son Nagappa died leaving behind his son Galappa.
Galappa also died leaving behind Venkataramanappa, Kemanna, Muniyappa and Hanumappa.
The fourth son Mudlappa died leaving behind Venkatarasappa @ Pachaiah and Mahadevappa.
.5. It is stated that the propositor Venkataramanappa and his sons constitute Hindu undivided co-parcenary joint family have inherited agricultural lands.
All the sons of Venkataramanappa are in joint possession and cultivation of the aforesaid lands.
Late. Venkataramanappa died intestate.

.6. It is stated that the claimants 7 and 8 have filed a suit in O.S. No.957/2001 on the file of Civil Judge (Sr.Dvn), Bengaluru for partition and separate possession of the aforesaid properties and they have L.A.C. No. 107/2014 C/w L.A.C. No. 108, 112 &113 of 2014 claimed 1/4th share in all the aforesaid properties.
The suit in O.S. No.957/2001 is disposed of on 16.11.2007 by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dvn) at Bengaluru.
Thereafter, RFA No.2608/2007 filed by the defendants before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The said RFA was disposed of on the basis of the compromise entered into between the parties by an order dated 15.02.2011.
By virtue of the compromise the claimant Nos.7 and 8 are entitled for 8 acres 22  guntas in the suit claim.
.7. The subject matter in the above claim petition is also included in the schedule to the plaint and RFA.
It is stated that out of the aforesaid properties some of the properties have been notified by the respondents for the acquisition of land for the purpose of BMIC project.
It is stated that the respondents having acquired the lands and on account of the objections filed by the claimants 7 and 8 the matter has been referred to this Court.

The claimants 7 and 8 are also entitled for share in the amount awarded by the respondents to an extent of 8 L.A.C. No. 107/2014 C/w L.A.C. No. 108, 112 &113 of 2014 acres 22  guntas of the total extent of the suit schedule.
It is stated that the claimants being the legal heirs are entitled to succeed to an extent of their 1/4th share in the amount awarded by the respondents in respepct of the property in question.
Hence, prayed to award compensation amount.

sentences.text: Subsequent to the compromise the claimants have not stated as to how they have divided the remaining items of suit schedule property.
The propositor Venkataramanappa had died leaving behind 4 sons.
The claimants are the legal heirs of the said 4 sons.
So, LRs of claimants 7 and claimant No.8 are together entitled for 1/4th compensation in the acquired land, which is as follows.
Hence, point No.1 is answered Partly in the affirmative.
.21. Point No.2:

The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.

The LRs of claimant No.7 and claimant No.8 are together entitled for compensation to the extent mentioned below in-respect of the property acquired in Sompura village with accrued interest thereon as follows:
L.A.C. No. 107/2014 C/w L.A.C. No. 108, 112 &113 of 2014 LAC No. Sy. The above claimants are entitled to interest under Section 34 of L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O. has to be deducted.
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO in-respect of other claimants is rejected.
Draw award accordingly.
